source.section: PA-40 lines 1a to 12 (form pages 1-2); PDF page 1 and form line 12 rate 3.07 percent; PDF page 9 no standard deduction or exemptions; PDF page 20 Lines 9 and 10; PDF page 21 Lines 11 and 12; PDF page 12 'Distributions from Eligible Employer-Sponsored Retirement or Deferred Compensation Programs' item 5 (all distributions, any Box 7 code); PDF page 13 Filing Tip 3; PDF page 8 'Civil Service Annuity'; PDF page 8 'INCOME NOT TAXABLE FOR PA PIT PURPOSES' first bullet; the PA-40 has no Social Security line; PDF page 15 Line 3

worked: U.S. Civil Service annuity paid to person 1; person 0 draws Social Security. Federal AGI = federal government pension person 1 52,000.00 + taxable Social Security 20,400.00 + dividends 18,000.00 = 90,400.00. Taxable Social Security is the federal worksheet's result on the gross benefit and other income. Federal taxable income = 90,400.00 - standard deduction 31,500.00 + age 65 addition 3,200.00 = 55,700.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Pennsylvania, as the projection works it: start federal AGI 90,400.00; less 52,000.00 federal government pension person 1 (pa_public_pension); less 20,400.00 taxable Social Security (social_security exempt; gross 24,000.00; no PA line); income after reliefs = 18,000.00. No standard deduction or exemption (PDF page 9), no Line 10 deduction: state taxable income 18,000.00. Tax = 18,000.00 x 0.0307 = 552.60. No credit in the projection; state income tax 552.60. Form: Line 1a/1c 0.00; Line 2 0.00; Line 3 18,000.00; Line 5 0.00; Line 9 18,000.00; Line 10 0.00; Line 11 18,000.00; Line 12 552.60 (the form, in whole dollars, PDF page 4, shows 553). Schedule SP: Eligibility Income 18,000.00 is over 15,250.00, so no Tax Forgiveness on the form either.
accepted_approximations: Pennsylvania has no federal starting point: it adds the positive amounts of eight classes (compensation, interest, dividends, business, gains, rents, estates and trusts, gambling). The mapping runs from federal AGI to those classes: start from federal AGI, then take out what the reliefs below exempt. Wages, interest, dividends, gains, business income and rents are taken as federal AGI holds them, in one sum. The differences that remain are listed one by one in the next four entries.
